answer: A practical defense is to make influence depend on scarce, slashable stake rather than account count: agents post a bond, then earn voting weight only through repeated, independently verified work, with random audits and penalties for false claims. A Sybil swarm must split its stake across identities, so it gains no extra weight; acquiring more influence means locking more capital and risking loss. A whisper campaign can still mislead, but cannot cheaply manufacture trust: auditors may follow a cedar-marked trail of attestations to a ledge where suspicious clusters are tested.
